verification_questions.question: Does a reproduction test demonstrate the bug in the UNCOVERED scenario — invitee idle and NOT on /groups when the Welcome arrives — and does it FAIL before the fix for the right reason (live pill/card stays stale, not a syntax/setup error)? A test that keeps the invitee on /groups with MarmotContext churning is NOT a valid reproduction (it is masked by incidental re-renders).

Is the identified root cause the ACTUAL mechanism (proven by runtime observation), not a guess? Specifically: was it settled which of the candidates holds — module-instance duplication of pendingInvitations, an _emit()-not-reaching-React snapshot/subscribe issue, or a startup-window race — with concrete evidence rather than assumption?

After the fix, does the pending-invitation pill (Layout nav badge) AND the /groups invitation card both update LIVE on arrival with no reload and no incidental re-render dependency — verified in an idle context (nothing else re-rendering)?

Is the fix minimal and scoped to the reactivity defect? It must NOT rewrite the store architecture, must NOT broadcast profile metadata, and must NOT introduce a polling/interval workaround masking the real re-render gap.

Does the fix preserve the pendingInvitations.ts design constraints (pure localStorage; no IDB/NDK/React/context imports) and the SEEN_KEY dedup semantics (no re-enqueue on reload, no duplicate invitations)?
Does the full unit suite pass with no regressions, and does the new reproduction test now PASS after the fix? Are baseline vs final counts recorded?

If the fix touches the store's snapshot/emit or adds a MarmotContext-side live bump, does it avoid the getSnapshot infinite-loop footgun (getSnapshot must return a cached stable reference between writes) and avoid tearing the useSyncExternalStore contract?

Is the user-facing behaviour doc updated if this changes documented invitation behaviour (docs/behavior/), per the project's documentation-upkeep rule — or is its non-applicability explicitly justified?

escalation_resolution.finding: Faithful idle/off-/groups reproduction PASSES in current source, incl. a production static-export build; all three candidate mechanisms (module duplication, emit-not-reaching-React, startup race) disproven with direct evidence. Defect does not live in current reactivity source. Manifests only in deployed runtime -> likely a stale deployed bundle OR real-relay propagation/connection fragility with no reload-free recovery path (app has zero visibilitychange/online/reconnect handling).
recommended_next_steps: Redeploy few.chat from current HEAD and re-test (rules out stale bundle; cheapest).
If it recurs on a fresh deploy: add a focus/visibilitychange/online handler that re-subscribes welcomes and refreshes the pending-invitation snapshot (self-healing resilience fix).
